edges.description: The fusion oncogene establishes an aberrant enhancer and super-enhancer transcriptional program that sits between the chromosomal fusion and phenotype-level outputs.
The fusion regulatory program induces ETS1 and intersects with KDM3A; this edge marks the entry into a feedback/cofactor module, not a claim that measured open chromatin causes the cofactor state.
Fusion-driven transcription induces an N-Myc feedback state in which N-Myc also activates PAX-FOXO1 expression and complexes with the fusion protein.
PAX3::FOXO1-mediated cell-cycle checkpoint adaptation creates a treatment-resistance branch mediated by the HDAC3-SMARCA4-miR-27a-PAX3::FOXO1 circuit.
Fusion-driven enhancer reprogramming impairs the terminal skeletal muscle differentiation program.
intermediate_mechanisms: suppression of terminal myogenic differentiation programs

edges.description: Fusion oncogene activity contributes to reduced antigen presentation and immune-cell infiltration, creating an immune-evasive tumor state.
intermediate_mechanisms: specific fusion-regulated immune-evasion targets remain incompletely resolved

edges.description: ETS1/KDM3A cofactor activity is modeled as a candidate maintenance input into the fusion-dependent enhancer program, not as a downstream consequence of the ATAC-seq accessibility measurement.

The cofactor module occupies and regulates disease-promoting enhancers including FGF8, which links the fusion/cofactor chromatin program to the FGF8/FGFR4 output branch. This does not by itself prove that FGFR signaling maintains the upstream chromatin state.
intermediate_mechanisms: PAX3-FOXO1/ETS1/KDM3A occupancy at the FGF8 enhancer
FGF8 expression in the FGFR4/FGF8 branch
FGFR4 phosphorylation in responsive fusion-positive RMS models

edges.description: Disrupting the PAX3-FOXO1/ETS1 complex inhibits growth and invasive properties, implying that this cofactor module sustains malignant tumor cell behavior.
intermediate_mechanisms: altered FGF8, IL4R, MEST, and PODXL expression

edges.description: Stabilizing PAX-FOXO1 and N-Myc is modeled as a feedback input into the fusion-dependent regulatory state. The cited work supports reciprocal transcriptional activation and malignancy dependence; whether the full ARMS open-chromatin signature collapses after YOD1 inhibition remains an explicit open test.
intermediate_mechanisms: YOD1-dependent PAX-FOXO1 and N-Myc protein stabilization

edges.description: YOD1-dependent stabilization of PAX-FOXO1 and N-Myc sustains FP-RMS growth.
intermediate_mechanisms: degradation of PAX-FOXO1 and N-Myc after YOD1 knockdown or inhibition

edges.description: The HDAC3-linked checkpoint adaptation circuit permits tumor cells to survive cytotoxic treatment pressure and contributes to relapse.

FGFR4 signaling is curated as an RTK input to downstream RAS-MAPK and PI3K-AKT effector arms. The canonical receptor-to-effector mechanism is supported, while ARMS-specific dependence remains context-dependent.

RAS-MAPK and PI3K-AKT effector pathway activation is modeled as a pro-proliferative and survival output of the RTK/RAS/PIK3CA axis. The edge preserves pathograph connectivity but remains qualified: the cited ARMS/RMS evidence supports recurrent pathway involvement, not a direct or universal ARMS-specific causal step.
Cancer-associated fibroblast secreted factors support fusion-positive RMS tumor-cell growth, migration, and treatment resistance.
Cancer-associated fibroblast support can add a microenvironmental treatment-resistance layer on top of tumor-cell-intrinsic resistance circuitry.

Fibroblast-supported migration is a plausible contributor to metastatic progression in fusion-positive RMS. The edge is deliberately indirect: the cited coculture study measures migration, while the clinical source establishes metastasis as a frequent outcome of the fusion-positive alveolar subtype.
Sustained malignant proliferation produces the soft-tissue tumor mass that defines rhabdomyosarcoma clinically. This is a disease-level output, not a claim about a particular primary anatomic site.
When the primary soft-tissue tumor is orbital, local tumor growth and mass effect can manifest as proptosis. This link applies to the orbital subset and is not an ARMS-wide frequency claim.
Local ARMS can spread through regional lymphatics. This is an indirect clinical edge and does not imply that every primary tumor develops nodal disease.
Parameningeal tumor growth can extend intracranially because of local anatomic continuity. This edge is restricted to the parameningeal subset.
intermediate_mechanisms: local invasion from a parameningeal primary

edges.description: Tests whether tumor-cell states can be redirected toward myogenic differentiation.
Tests CAF-mediated growth and treatment-resistance effects.

nodes.description: Malignant growth is the convergent output of multiple now-explicit upstream mechanisms: PAX-FOXO1 enhancer reprogramming, ETS1/KDM3A chromatin cofactor dependence, YOD1/N-Myc feedback and protein stabilization, FGFR/RAS/PI3K signaling, and treatment-resistant relapse states.

evidence.reference_title: Therapeutic targeting of YOD1 disrupts the PAX-FOXO1/N-Myc feedback loop in rhabdomyosarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Knocking down YOD1 or inhibiting it with G5 could suppress FP-RMS growth both in vitro and in vivo, through promoting the degradation of both PAX-FOXO1 and N-Myc.

nodes.description: Fusion-driven transcriptional and enhancer reprogramming impairs the normal terminal myogenic differentiation program. Tumor cells retain skeletal muscle lineage markers but remain trapped in a malignant, incompletely differentiated state.

evidence.reference_title: Molecular Targets in Alveolar Rhabdomyosarcoma: A Narrative Review of Progress and Pitfalls.
evidence.snippet: We discuss the central role of fusion proteins in transcriptional reprogramming, impaired myogenic differentiation, and super-enhancer activation.

experimental_models.description: Tests whether tumor-cell states can be redirected toward myogenic differentiation.
experimental_models.name: Patient-derived ARMS single-cell culture model

evidence.reference_title: Gene Amplification in Rhabdomyosarcoma: Lessons from a Rare Cancer.
evidence.snippet: amplification of the 12q13-q14 chromosomal region involves a gene-rich region in which there are at least two critical protein-coding oncogenic targets (CDK4 and SHMT2).

nodes.description: A clinically important disease state in which initially chemotherapy- responsive PAX3::FOXO1-positive ARMS survives treatment pressure, relapses, and becomes resistant. In this pathograph it is modeled as a downstream output of specific mechanisms, especially the HDAC3-SMARCA4-miR-27a checkpoint-adaptation circuit and microenvironmental support, rather than as an unexplained late clinical outcome.

evidence.reference_title: Entinostat as a combinatorial therapeutic for rhabdomyosarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Metastatic PAX3::FOXO1+ ARMS often responds to chemotherapies initially, only to subsequently relapse and become resistant with most patients failing to survive beyond 8 years post-diagnosis.

nodes.description: KDM3A and ETS1 form a disease-promoting chromatin cofactor axis with PAX3-FOXO1. ETS1 is induced by PAX3-FOXO1 and KDM3A, complexes with PAX3-FOXO1, augments fusion occupancy at enhancers, and helps maintain disease-promoting target genes including FGF8, IL4R, MEST, and PODXL. This is a direct mechanistic handle because YK-4-279 disrupts the PAX3-FOXO1/ETS1 complex and displaces PAX3-FOXO1 from chromatin.

evidence.reference_title: Dependence of PAX3-FOXO1 chromatin occupancy on ETS1 at important disease-promoting genes exposes new targetable vulnerability in Fusion-Positive Rhabdomyosarcoma.
evidence.snippet: We show that ETS1, which is induced by both PAX3-FOXO1 and KDM3A, exists in complex with PAX3-FOXO1, and augments PAX3-FOXO1 chromatin occupancy.

nodes.description: Investigational FGFR-directed therapy may be relevant in fusion-positive ARMS with high FGFR4/FGF8 signaling activity. Preclinical models and early translational evidence support FGFR4-selective and multikinase FGFR inhibition as precision-therapy approaches in this molecular subset.

evidence.reference_title: Comprehensive Multiplatform Tyrosine Kinase Profiling Reveals Novel Actionable FGFR Aberrations across Sarcomas Affecting the Young.
evidence.snippet: We demonstrate marked tumor growth inhibition in all FP-RMS PDXs treated with single-agent FGF401 (FGFR4-specific inhibitor) and single-agent lenvatinib (multikinase FGFR inhibitor)

evidence.reference_title: Comprehensive Multiplatform Tyrosine Kinase Profiling Reveals Novel Actionable FGFR Aberrations across Sarcomas Affecting the Young.
evidence.snippet: report a clinical response to lenvatinib in a patient with relapsed metastatic FP-RMS.

nodes.description: One branch of the fusion-positive ARMS program is receptor tyrosine kinase signaling centered on FGFR4, driven by high FGFR4 and FGF8 expression and FGFR4 phosphoactivation. This is a directly druggable downstream output branch, not currently a proven maintainer of the upstream fusion-dependent chromatin state.

biological_processes: fibroblast growth factor receptor signaling pathway

evidence.reference_title: Comprehensive Multiplatform Tyrosine Kinase Profiling Reveals Novel Actionable FGFR Aberrations across Sarcomas Affecting the Young.
evidence.snippet: We highlight the utility of FGFR inhibitors in PAX3-FOXO1 fusion-positive rhabdomyosarcomas (FP-RMS) characterized by high FGFR4 and FGF8 RNA expression levels and FGFR4 activation (FGFR4_pY).

nodes.description: A human coculture model tests fibroblast-secreted support of FP-RMS growth, migration, immune-checkpoint expression, and cyclophosphamide resistance. It represents one metastatic microenvironment and does not establish the prevalence of this state across patients.

evidence.reference_title: Cancer-associated fibroblasts promote tumor progression in fusion-positive rhabdomyosarcoma.
evidence.snippet: This study establishes a model of cancer-associated fibroblasts from metastatic fusion-positive rhabdomyosarcoma.

nodes.description: PAX3::FOXO1-mediated cell-cycle checkpoint adaptation creates a relapse and chemotherapy-resistance branch mediated by an HDAC3-SMARCA4-miR-27a-PAX3::FOXO1 circuit. This is the mechanistic target of HDAC3-directed epigenetic therapy with entinostat-like class I HDAC inhibition, not merely a generic "HDAC inhibitor" rationale.

evidence.reference_title: Entinostat as a combinatorial therapeutic for rhabdomyosarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Chemotherapy resistance in ARMS has previously been attributed to PAX3::FOXO1-mediated cell cycle checkpoint adaptation, which is mediated by an HDAC3-SMARCA4-miR-27a-PAX3::FOXO1 circuit that can be disrupted by HDAC3 inhibition.

nodes.description: Investigational class I histone deacetylase inhibition, exemplified by entinostat in PAX3::FOXO1-positive ARMS PDX models, targets the HDAC3-SMARCA4-miR-27a-PAX3::FOXO1 chemotherapy-resistance circuit and may resensitize relapsed or resistant disease to RMS chemotherapy.

evidence.reference_title: Entinostat as a combinatorial therapeutic for rhabdomyosarcoma.
evidence.snippet: We identified single agent, additive or synergistic relationships between relapse-specific chemotherapies and clinically relevant drug exposures of entinostat in three PAX3::FOXO1+ ARMS mouse models.

nodes.description: Fusion-positive rhabdomyosarcoma can develop an immune-cold and fibroblast-supported tumor microenvironment, with reduced T-cell infiltration, impaired antigen presentation, immune-checkpoint expression, cancer-associated fibroblast cytokine support, and resistance to chemotherapy or immunotherapy.

evidence.reference_title: Tumor-Immune Interactions in Pediatric Oral Rhabdomyosarcoma: A Narrative Review on Immuno-Oncology and Emerging Therapies.
evidence.snippet: Additionally, the presence of fusion oncogenes, such as PAX3:FOXO1, hampers immunogenicity and treatment response by disrupting antigen presentation and reducing immune cell infiltration.

evidence.reference_title: Cancer-associated fibroblasts promote tumor progression in fusion-positive rhabdomyosarcoma.
evidence.snippet: The cancer-associated fibroblasts also promoted expression of immune checkpoints and conferred resistance to cyclophosphamide, a chemotherapy commonly used to treat this disease.

experimental_models.description: Tests CAF-mediated growth and treatment-resistance effects.
experimental_models.name: Fusion-positive RMS cancer-associated fibroblast coculture

nodes.description: Intracranial extension occurs in a subset of parameningeal ARMS and is an adverse prognostic feature. This site-specific cohort estimate is not generalized to ARMS at other primary sites, and no overly broad HPO term is assigned.

evidence.reference_title: Patterns of Failure in Parameningeal Alveolar Rhabdomyosarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Most patients had group III (96%), node-negative (67%), positive FOX fusion status (63%) disease, and intracranial extension (54%).

evidence.reference_title: Comprehensive genomic analysis of rhabdomyosarcoma reveals a landscape of alterations affecting a common genetic axis in fusion-positive and fusion-negative tumors.
evidence.snippet: Amplification of 2p24 involving MYCN (5%) occurred predominantly in PFP tumors (8 PFP vs. 1 PFN)

nodes.description: Metastasis and recurrence are major clinical features of fusion-positive ARMS. Their incidence varies by fusion status, primary site, stage, and ascertainment time, so this entry does not assign a single frequency band.

evidence.reference_title: Cancer-associated fibroblasts promote tumor progression in fusion-positive rhabdomyosarcoma.
evidence.snippet: The PAX3/PAX7-FOXO1 fusion-positive alveolar subtype has poor clinical outcomes, with frequent recurrence, metastasis, and low survival.

evidence.reference_title: Patterns of Failure in Parameningeal Alveolar Rhabdomyosarcoma.
evidence.snippet: All 7 patients with distant metastases as the first site of recurrence had central nervous system metastases.

nodes.description: PAX-FOXO1 does not act as a generic "oncogene" in the pathograph; it rewires chromatin occupancy, enhancer activity, and transcriptional output. This node is the inferred regulatory program, not the ATAC-seq/open chromatin measurement itself. Disease-specific open chromatin is an assayable projection of this program and can be used to test whether perturbing candidate maintenance machinery changes the regulatory state itself, as opposed to changing downstream or branch-specific outputs such as FGFR signaling, immune evasion, or chemotherapy resistance.

evidence.reference_title: Molecular Targets in Alveolar Rhabdomyosarcoma: A Narrative Review of Progress and Pitfalls.
evidence.snippet: We discuss the central role of fusion proteins in transcriptional reprogramming, impaired myogenic differentiation, and super-enhancer activation.

nodes.description: The t(2;13) or t(1;13) translocations fuse the DNA-binding domain of PAX3 or PAX7 with the transactivation domain of FOXO1. The resulting fusion protein functions as a potent aberrant transcription factor that activates PAX target genes to supraphysiological levels, driving proliferation while blocking terminal myogenic differentiation.

biological_processes: positive regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II

evidence.reference_title: [Characteristics of the cytogenetic variants of alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma].
evidence.snippet: According to literature data, the frequency of the PAX3::FOXO1 translocation is 70-90% and the PAX7::FOXO1 translocation 10-30%.

evidence.reference_title: Comprehensive genomic analysis of rhabdomyosarcoma reveals a landscape of alterations affecting a common genetic axis in fusion-positive and fusion-negative tumors.
evidence.snippet: As expected, the defining genomic alteration seen across the entire cohort was recurrent t(2;13) or t(1;13), that resulted in a fusion of the N-terminus of PAX3 or PAX7 to the C-terminus of FOXO1

nodes.description: Investigational small-molecule disruption of the PAX3-FOXO1/ETS1 complex is a direct chromatin-handle strategy: it aims to displace PAX3-FOXO1 from disease enhancers and suppress fusion-dependent gene regulation rather than treating the fusion as an untargetable upstream abstraction.

evidence.reference_title: Dependence of PAX3-FOXO1 chromatin occupancy on ETS1 at important disease-promoting genes exposes new targetable vulnerability in Fusion-Positive Rhabdomyosarcoma.
evidence.snippet: We further show that the PAX3-FOXO1/ETS1 complex can be disrupted by the clinically relevant small molecule inhibitor YK-4-279.

evidence.reference_title: [Characteristics of the cytogenetic variants of alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma].
evidence.snippet: According to literature data, the frequency of the PAX3::FOXO1 translocation is 70-90% and the PAX7::FOXO1 translocation 10-30%.

evidence.reference_title: [Characteristics of the cytogenetic variants of alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma].
evidence.snippet: According to literature data, the frequency of the PAX3::FOXO1 translocation is 70-90% and the PAX7::FOXO1 translocation 10-30%.

evidence.reference_title: PAX3/FOXO1 fusion gene status is the key prognostic molecular marker in rhabdomyosarcoma and significantly improves current risk stratification.
evidence.snippet: Among nonmetastatic patients, patients who were PAX3/FOXO1 positive had a significantly poorer outcome compared with both alveolar-negative and PAX7/FOXO1-positive patients.

nodes.description: Patient-derived aRMS cultures resolve cycling progenitor, muscle stem-like, and differentiated states and enable perturbational testing of RAF/MEK inhibitors. Culture-state findings require confirmation in clinical tumors.

evidence.reference_title: Single-cell profiling of alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma reveals RAS pathway inhibitors as cell-fate hijackers with therapeutic relevance.
evidence.snippet: Here, we combined single-cell RNA sequencing, mass cytometry, and high-content imaging to resolve intratumoral heterogeneity of patient-derived primary RMS cultures.

nodes.description: Orbital rhabdomyosarcoma can present with eyelid edema followed by proptosis. The cited cohort includes both pediatric and adult orbital RMS and does not establish an ARMS-specific frequency.

evidence.reference_title: Adult and pediatric orbital rhabdomyosarcoma: comparison of characteristics and outcomes.
evidence.snippet: Patients in both groups presented with eyelid edema followed by proptosis with similar symptom duration (p = 0.31).

nodes.description: Receptor tyrosine kinase input converges on the downstream RAS-MAPK and PI3K-AKT effector pathways. Genomic profiling shows the combined RTK/RAS/PIK3CA axis is altered in the large majority of rhabdomyosarcomas; this effector branch is therefore a curated downstream signaling state, not a claim that RAS/PI3K activation is the only or universal route to ARMS proliferation.

evidence.reference_title: Comprehensive genomic analysis of rhabdomyosarcoma reveals a landscape of alterations affecting a common genetic axis in fusion-positive and fusion-negative tumors.
evidence.snippet: Furthermore, alteration of the receptor tyrosine kinase/RAS/PIK3CA axis affects 93% of cases, providing a framework for genomics-directed therapies that might improve outcomes for patients with rhabdomyosarcoma.

nodes.description: Regional lymph-node involvement is a clinically important staging and prognostic feature in ARMS. The cited cohort is limited to parameningeal disease; no page-wide frequency is assigned. No sufficiently specific HPO term for regional nodal metastasis is used in place of the broader lymphadenopathy phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: Patterns of Failure in Parameningeal Alveolar Rhabdomyosarcoma.
evidence.snippet: N1 disease and intracranial extension (ICE) portended inferior overall survival (P = .002 and .02, respectively).

nodes.description: ARMS is a pediatric soft-tissue sarcoma; the local presentation depends on the primary anatomic site. A mass should therefore trigger tissue diagnosis rather than serve as a subtype-specific finding by itself.

evidence.reference_title: Molecular Targets in Alveolar Rhabdomyosarcoma: A Narrative Review of Progress and Pitfalls.
evidence.snippet: Alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma (ARMS) is a highly aggressive pediatric soft-tissue sarcoma driven by PAX3/7-FOXO1 fusion proteins.

nodes.description: Investigational YOD1 inhibition is modeled as a feedback-loop intervention: inhibiting YOD1 destabilizes both PAX-FOXO1 and N-Myc, reducing the reciprocal oncogenic amplification loop rather than targeting only a downstream proliferation phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: Therapeutic targeting of YOD1 disrupts the PAX-FOXO1/N-Myc feedback loop in rhabdomyosarcoma.
evidence.snippet: Knocking down YOD1 or inhibiting it with G5 could suppress FP-RMS growth both in vitro and in vivo, through promoting the degradation of both PAX-FOXO1 and N-Myc.

nodes.description: N-Myc is both a downstream target and a reciprocal activator of PAX-FOXO1. YOD1 stabilizes both PAX-FOXO1 and N-Myc, maintaining a positive feedback loop that amplifies oncogenic signaling. This creates a second targetable handle upstream of generic proliferation: destabilize the two oncogenic proteins together rather than treating N-Myc as only a downstream proliferation marker.

evidence.reference_title: Therapeutic targeting of YOD1 disrupts the PAX-FOXO1/N-Myc feedback loop in rhabdomyosarcoma.
evidence.snippet: We further identified YOD1 as a deubiquitinating enzyme that stabilizes both PAX-FOXO1 and N-Myc.
